Hi Emma — thanks, great to hear the demo was helpful. High level answers below; detailed follow-up from our infra team is in the next message.

- EU-pin model: We offer an "anchored placement" configuration. For strict anchoring we can run control and data plane components in EU-only cloud regions and disable scheduled telemetry exports. That said, we do have documented bounded-failover behaviors (we call these "conditional egress windows") that customers can opt into or out of in the DPA annex.

- Conditional egress triggers: We enumerate three trigger classes in our policy: DR (region-wide hardware or AZ outage with documented failover tests), court/legal process with valid service of process, and security incident requiring cross-region analysis (e.g., forensic image collection). Each trigger requires a two-party approval: customer security officer (email confirmation) + Redwood ops on-call. All events produce an immutable audit record and token-level access is minimized via redaction and sampling wherever possible. Keys are customer-managed via KMS where required — EU KMS is supported.

- Subprocessors: Short answer: telemetry and analytics pipeline processors are hosted by our cloud partners (region-local) and two analytics vendors we contract with. Karthik will list the vendors and the exact signal types.

I'll loop in Karthik and Laura for technical and contractual specifics so you have text you can paste into the DPA redline.

Best,
Olga

Hi Emma, adding the infra specifics you asked for — I kept the wording DPA-ready: 

1) Maximum durations (per trigger):
  - Disaster Recovery (DR): up to 48 hours of cross-region processing for in-flight KV/cache rehydration and model checkpoint streaming. Any DR window beyond 48 hours requires mutual written authorization (email to security@redwood.example.com + customer security contact).
  - Legal Compulsion: processing necessary to comply with lawful request; duration is limited to the scope of the request. We will refuse overly broad requests and notify the customer unless prohibited.
  - Security Forensics: up to 14 calendar days for snapshot collection and analysis. Extensions require customer approval or a court order.

2) Audit trail fields & retention:
  - Fields captured: trigger_type, trigger_initiator (Redwood ops/customer/legal), UTC timestamps (triggered_at, approved_at, completed_at), authorizing_emails, affected_object_paths (S3 key prefixes), summary_of_data_types_accessed (e.g., token-level logs: sampled/redacted), KMS_key_id_used, and a short redaction hash.
  - Retention: audit records retained for 2 years by default; can be extended per contract. Audit artifacts (forensic snapshots) retained per customer agreement — default 90 days unless otherwise requested.

3) KMS and keys:
  - Yes, Redwood supports customer-supplied EU KMS (bring-your-own-key) with key material never exported outside EU.
  - During a bounded failover we may use ephemeral, service-side keys for internal orchestration, but customer-controlled keys remain authoritative for decryption. Ephemeral keys are generated in-region where possible; if cross-region generation is necessary we will record the event in the audit trail and limit exposure to metadata only (no plaintext).

4) Subprocessors & data visibility:
  - Current roster (short): Cloud provider region-local telemetry, AnalyticaOps Ltd (telemetry summarization, EU-based), and Metricly (ops metrics ingestion).
  - Data types: aggregated telemetry, sampled logs with prompt/response redaction, and anonymized latency/usage metrics. We do not share full token streams with external vendors for anchored customers unless mutual approval is granted for forensic purposes.

I've attached a one-page "residency matrix" that you can drop into the DPA annex and a suggested DPA clause for the conditional egress window.

—Karthik
